title: Throughput-aware progressive bundler with KV prefetch and slab-aware placement
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Implement and evaluate a progressive bundler (PB) for streaming chat completions that balances latency SLOs and throughput by combining: 1) a lightweight predictive bundling policy that groups near-term turns, 2) KV-cache prefetch scheduling to reduce cold-KV stalls, and 3) slab-aware placement to reduce GPU memory fragmentation. The intent is to increase token/sec on overloaded GPUs while keeping 95th-p99 latency regressions within 10% of baseline for interactive clients.
acceptance_criteria: 1) PB reduces average GPU tokens/sec variance by >= 20% under 200% traffic bursts compared to current windowed bundler. 2) Cold-KV miss rate reduced by >= 30% for multi-turn sessions with >4 turns. 3) End-to-end median latency for streaming chat stays within +5% and p95 within +12% of baseline on test cluster. 4) Feature gated behind runtime flag and can be disabled without rolling restarts.
technical_notes: Heuristics: - Progressive bundler forms a micro-batch for streaming completions by combining (a) recent-turn affinity (time delta < X ms), (b) predicted completion length bands from a tiny LR model on request metadata, and (c) per-client latency budget. - KV prefetch scheduler tags chosen sessions and loads their KV pages into GPU memory ahead of the dispatch window; priority based on predicted token cost and recency. - Slab-aware placement uses current slab occupancy map (coarse-grained) to place new KV pages into least-fragmenting slab; evictions prefer cold shards with high rehydrate cost threshold. - Memory signal inputs: live GPU free bytes, slab fragmentation score, estimated KV page footprint per session. - Fallback: if prefetch budget exceeded, fall back to on-demand fetch and mark session as low-priority for subsequent bundles.
decisions: 1) Use 3-tier prediction (short/medium/long) instead of fine-grained token counts to keep model tiny and inference cheap. 2) Prefetch budget is expressed in bytes per-GPU and enforced by token-budget window; prefetch reservations expire after 60s. 3) Implement slabbing at 16MB granularity to reduce allocator complexity. 4) Initial rollout gated to non-critical customers and experimental cluster.
updates: 2026-02-16: Spike completed — profiled common conversation shapes and KV miss patterns across a 48h production window. Observed high KV miss cost for multi-turn assistants with frequent short completions.

2026-02-20: Prototype bundler implemented (pushed to feature branch). Microbenchmarks show 12% throughput improvement on synthetic burst workload but increased p95 latency by ~9% in worst-case if prefetch not tuned.
2026-02-24: Added slab occupancy telemetry and eviction scoring. Early numbers: fragmentation reduced by ~18% versus naive allocator under mixed workloads.
2026-02-28: Integration tests with streaming path passed in CI. Launch checklist items created: config flag, perf dashboards, canary rollout plan.

2026-03-01: Running canary on two experimental clusters for 72h. Observed: cold-KV miss rate down 35% for target sessions; overall 95th latency trending +8% under extreme concurrency; throttles introduced when prefetch budget is hit.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for bundler decision logic and prefetch scheduler. 2) Integration e2e harness simulating mixed conversational workloads (short-heavy, long-sparse). 3) Load test across 3 cluster shapes: small (4xA10), medium (8xA100), large (16xA100). Measure median/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, KV miss rate, GPU memory fragmentation. 4) Canary rollout to 2 experimental clusters for 72h, monitor console dashboards and circuit-breaker metrics.
risks_mitigation: Risk: Over-aggressive prefetch increases memory pressure and causes OOMs. Mitigation: enforce per-GPU prefetch byte budget and conservative default (20% of free memory). Risk: Prediction model mislabels long completions causing deadline misses. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds with rapid decay to avoid growing bundles, and a hard cap on micro-batch size. Risk: Increased p95 latency for interactive customers. Mitigation: runtime flag to route latency-sensitive customer traffic to baseline bundler and canary metrics to halt rollout automatically.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on the eviction scoring function and the prefetch budget enforcement. Look for any hidden race between slab placement and KV streaming eviction. Also validate that the roll-out plan includes observability hooks for per-session bundle decisions.
